findings.body:
Disabling `verify_signature`, `verify_aud`, and `verify_iss` makes `identity()` trust any token payload. An attacker can mint an unsigned JWT (or one signed with an arbitrary key) and obtain any `sub`/roles the app reads from the decoded dict.

The comment cites a temporary staging migration (TICKET-412), but nothing scopes this to staging: there is no env check, config flag, or fail-closed default. Merging this into a shared `auth.py` disables authentication for every deployment that imports it.

Restore verification with the real signing key (or a dual-key accept during rotation). If an emergency bypass is unavoidable, gate it explicitly on a non-production environment and keep `audience`/`issuer` checks enabled even then.

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge.** This change disables JWT signature, audience, and issuer verification for every caller of `identity()`, which means any client can forge a token and assume any identity.

## Why this is blocking

`jwt.decode(..., options={"verify_signature": False, "verify_aud": False, "verify_iss": False})` accepts unsigned or arbitrarily signed payloads. The PR description frames this as a temporary staging unblock for TICKET-412, but the code has **no environment, feature-flag, or host gate** — the same path would run wherever this module is deployed.

The previous contract (`SECRET` + `HS256` + fixed `audience`/`issuer`) is removed entirely. `SECRET` remains in the module but is no longer used, so re-enabling verification is not automatic when tokens are re-issued.

## Recommendation

Keep verification on. If staging tokens truly cannot validate until re-issuance, use a staging-only key/issuer rotation, dual-key accept during migration, or an explicit non-production guard that fails closed in prod — never global `verify_signature: False`.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: The patch removes SECRET/algorithms/audience/issuer from jwt.decode and sets verify_signature, verify_aud, and verify_iss all to False with only a TICKET-412 comment and no env/config gate, so any unsigned or arbitrarily signed token payload is trusted.
